The Guilds

#Two numbers per guild||-Earn Reputation as you play. You never spend it; it alone sets your rank.||-It falls through rival earnings, a demand you let expire, a bounty you took and failed, and the upkeep each guild charges to keep you on its books.||-You earn Favour alongside Reputation and spend it on services. Spending Favour never lowers your rank.||#The five ranks||-Unmarked 0 / Indebted 100 / Sworn 300 / Favoured 700 / Exalted 1500||-Each rank grants a bonus for as long as you hold it. The Guilds tab shows your current bonus.||#Services||-Each guild sells three services. Each needs a rank, costs Favour and has a cooldown.||-Prices change with your Reputation: a guild that knows you charges less; one whose rival you court charges more.
Earning

#What each guild pays for||-The Brass Tablets: income each turn||-The Immortals: battles won, doubled when outnumbered||-The Daemonsmiths: technologies completed||-The Khanate: successful hero actions||-The Overseers: settlement growth and buildings no other guild claims||-The Slavers: sacking settlements; razing pays more||-The Temple of Hashut: loyal provinces, wins over the Dwarfs||-Completing a building pays its guild: a forge the Daemonsmiths, a dock the Brass Tablets, a barracks the Immortals. Higher levels pay more. The building card names its guild.||-Completing any mission raises your Reputation with every guild.||#Rivalry||-Brass Tablets and Khanate / Immortals and Daemonsmiths / Overseers and Slavers||-Earning with one takes Reputation from its rival once you reach Indebted there, but never a rank.||#A limit each turn||-Most guilds limit earnings each turn. The Guilds tab shows what each paid.
Bounties

#The board||-Three offers at a time, drawn from all guilds. Accept one to make it a mission.||-Accepting costs a Favour stake with that guild, shown on the offer. Finish the bounty to reclaim it; fail or hand it back and you lose it.||-Finish the bounty for gold and a large Reputation reward from that guild.||#What the guilds ask for||-Targets: land or a lord far from your borders and armies, or one belonging to a faction at peace with you. Taking that one means war, and pays far more.||-Other jobs: hold gold, raise a champion, research, build one of the guild's own buildings, or take captives.||-Or hero work: send your heroes against a named settlement, army or character.||#The price||-Target and distance set the price: Routine, Hard or Grim. An offer changes price until you accept it. Once accepted, it keeps its price.
The Court

#Leading a guild||-The faction with the most Reputation in a guild leads it, whether you or a rival.||-The leader gains an extra bonus. Unless the settings say otherwise, only the leader can buy the guild's finest service.||-It can be taken from you. The Leaderboard tab shows who leads each guild.||#Demands||-From time to time, a guild that knows you makes a demand with a deadline.||-It asks for gold or Favour held with its rival.||-Pay it to gain Reputation. Miss the deadline and your Reputation falls, which can cost you a rank.||#A patron||-Appoint one of your lords to a guild. Select them on the campaign map, then press Appoint.||-Their army gains +10% replenishment and +10% campaign movement.||-You earn 50% more Reputation with that guild, and its services cost up to 10% less.||-One lord, one guild. A new appointment replaces the old one.
Losing Reputation

#Reputation can fall||-You never spend Reputation, but four things reduce it. Three can cost you a rank and its bonus.||#Upkeep, every turn||-After the opening turns, each guild you have Reputation with takes a little of it back each turn.||-Higher ranks cost more upkeep. Stop earning with a guild and you lose ranks over time.||-The Guilds tab shows upkeep in red beside your Reputation.||#Earning with a rival||-Earning with a guild takes Reputation from its rival, though never a rank you have reached. You cannot court them all at once.||#A demand you let expire||-The Court tab shows the terms and deadline. Ignoring it costs more than the demand asked for.||#A bounty you took and failed||-Handing one back costs your Favour stake.||-Failing one costs the stake and Reputation. Each card shows how much.
Your race

#Services change||-Every ten turns, unless the settings say otherwise, each guild changes its three services. The footer counts down to the next change.||-A service keeps its cooldown while away and shows the time left when it returns.||#Services of your own||-Only your race can buy Conclave Backing, Hell-Forge Allotment and Labour Gangs, each marked Chaos Dwarf on its card. At least one is always available.||#What else pays||-A convoy that reaches its destination pays the Brass Tablets.||#Race rule||-Hashut's tithe: the guilds make demands more often, and a demand you pay is worth half again as much.||-Turn off Race differences in the settings to remove all this: every race plays alike.
Guild halls

#Guild halls||-Build guild halls in your settlements. The Guilds

#Two numbers per guild||-Earn Reputation as you play. You never spend it; it alone sets your rank.||-It falls through rival earnings, a demand you let expire, a bounty you took and failed, and the upkeep each guild charges to keep you on its books.||-You earn Favour alongside Reputation and spend it on services. Spending Favour never lowers your rank.||#The five ranks||-Outsider 0 / Apprentice 100 / Journeyman 300 / Master 700 / Grand Master 1500||-Each rank grants a bonus for as long as you hold it. The Guilds tab shows your current bonus.||#Services||-Each guild sells three services. Each needs a rank, costs Favour and has a cooldown.||-Prices change with your Reputation: a guild that knows you charges less; one whose rival you court charges more.
Earning

#What each guild pays for||-The Merchant Guilds: income each turn||-The Greatswords: battles won, doubled when outnumbered||-The Engineers' School: technologies completed||-The Thieves' Guild: successful hero actions||-The Masons' Guild: settlement growth and buildings no other guild claims||-The Free Companies: sacking settlements; razing pays more||-The Colleges of Magic: clean provinces, wizards' actions||-Completing a building pays its guild: a forge the Engineers' School, a dock the Merchant Guilds, a barracks the Greatswords. Higher levels pay more. The building card names its guild.||-Completing any mission raises your Reputation with every guild.||#Rivalry||-Merchant Guilds and Thieves' Guild / Greatswords and Engineers' School / Masons' Guild and Free Companies||-Earning with one takes Reputation from its rival once you reach Apprentice there, but never a rank.||#A limit each turn||-Most guilds limit earnings each turn. The Guilds tab shows what each paid.
Bounties

#The board||-Three offers at a time, drawn from all guilds. Accept one to make it a mission.||-Accepting costs a Favour stake with that guild, shown on the offer. Finish the bounty to reclaim it; fail or hand it back and you lose it.||-Finish the bounty for gold and a large Reputation reward from that guild.||#What the guilds ask for||-Targets: land or a lord far from your borders and armies, or one belonging to a faction at peace with you. Taking that one means war, and pays far more.||-Other jobs: hold gold, raise a champion, research, build one of the guild's own buildings, or take captives.||-Or hero work: send your heroes against a named settlement, army or character.||#The price||-Target and distance set the price: Routine, Hard or Grim. An offer changes price until you accept it. Once accepted, it keeps its price.
The Court

#Leading a guild||-The faction with the most Reputation in a guild leads it, whether you or a rival.||-The leader gains an extra bonus. Unless the settings say otherwise, only the leader can buy the guild's finest service.||-It can be taken from you. The Leaderboard tab shows who leads each guild.||#Demands||-From time to time, a guild that knows you makes a demand with a deadline.||-It asks for gold or Favour held with its rival.||-Pay it to gain Reputation. Miss the deadline and your Reputation falls, which can cost you a rank.||#A patron||-Appoint one of your lords to a guild. Select them on the campaign map, then press Appoint.||-Their army gains +10% replenishment and +10% campaign movement.||-You earn 50% more Reputation with that guild, and its services cost up to 10% less.||-One lord, one guild. A new appointment replaces the old one.
Losing Reputation

#Reputation can fall||-You never spend Reputation, but four things reduce it. Three can cost you a rank and its bonus.||#Upkeep, every turn||-After the opening turns, each guild you have Reputation with takes a little of it back each turn.||-Higher ranks cost more upkeep. Stop earning with a guild and you lose ranks over time.||-The Guilds tab shows upkeep in red beside your Reputation.||#Earning with a rival||-Earning with a guild takes Reputation from its rival, though never a rank you have reached. You cannot court them all at once.||#A demand you let expire||-The Court tab shows the terms and deadline. Ignoring it costs more than the demand asked for.||#A bounty you took and failed||-Handing one back costs your Favour stake.||-Failing one costs the stake and Reputation. Each card shows how much.
Your race

#Services change||-Every ten turns, unless the settings say otherwise, each guild changes its three services. The footer counts down to the next change.||-A service keeps its cooldown while away and shows the time left when it returns.||#Services of your own||-Only your race can buy The Watch-Houses, Elector's Muster and Unity of the Empire, each marked Empire on its card. Guild halls

#Guild halls||-Build guild halls in your settlements. The Guilds

#Two numbers per guild||-Earn Reputation as you play. You never spend it; it alone sets your rank.||-It falls through rival earnings, a demand you let expire, a bounty you took and failed, and the upkeep each guild charges to keep you on its books.||-You earn Favour alongside Reputation and spend it on services. Spending Favour never lowers your rank.||#The five ranks||-Stranger 0 / Beardling 100 / Oathsworn 300 / Longbeard 700 / Elder 1500||-Each rank grants a bonus for as long as you hold it. The Guilds tab shows your current bonus.||#Services||-Each guild sells three services. Each needs a rank, costs Favour and has a cooldown.||-Prices change with your Reputation: a guild that knows you charges less; one whose rival you court charges more.
Earning

#What each guild pays for||-The Merchant Clans: income each turn||-The Hammerers: battles won, doubled when outnumbered||-The Engineers' Guild: technologies completed||-The Rangers: successful hero actions||-The Miners' Guild: settlement growth and buildings no other guild claims||-The Grudge-Settlers: sacking settlements; razing pays more||-The Ancestor Temples: loyal provinces, wins over greenskins and skaven||-Completing a building pays its guild: a forge the Engineers' Guild, a dock the Merchant Clans, a barracks the Hammerers. Higher levels pay more. The building card names its guild.||-Completing any mission raises your Reputation with every guild.||#Rivalry||-Merchant Clans and Rangers / Hammerers and Engineers' Guild / Miners' Guild and Grudge-Settlers||-Earning with one takes Reputation from its rival once you reach Beardling there, but never a rank.||#A limit each turn||-Most guilds limit earnings each turn. The Guilds tab shows what each paid.
Bounties

#The board||-Three offers at a time, drawn from all guilds. Accept one to make it a mission.||-Accepting costs a Favour stake with that guild, shown on the offer. Finish the bounty to reclaim it; fail or hand it back and you lose it.||-Finish the bounty for gold and a large Reputation reward from that guild.||#What the guilds ask for||-Targets: land or a lord far from your borders and armies, or one belonging to a faction at peace with you. Taking that one means war, and pays far more.||-Other jobs: hold gold, raise a champion, research, build one of the guild's own buildings, or take captives.||-Or hero work: send your heroes against a named settlement, army or character.||#The price||-Target and distance set the price: Routine, Hard or Grim. An offer changes price until you accept it. Once accepted, it keeps its price.
The Court

#Leading a guild||-The faction with the most Reputation in a guild leads it, whether you or a rival.||-The leader gains an extra bonus. Unless the settings say otherwise, only the leader can buy the guild's finest service.||-It can be taken from you. The Leaderboard tab shows who leads each guild.||#Demands||-From time to time, a guild that knows you makes a demand with a deadline.||-It asks for gold or Favour held with its rival.||-Pay it to gain Reputation. Miss the deadline and your Reputation falls, which can cost you a rank.||#A patron||-Appoint one of your lords to a guild. Select them on the campaign map, then press Appoint.||-Their army gains +10% replenishment and +10% campaign movement.||-You earn 50% more Reputation with that guild, and its services cost up to 10% less.||-One lord, one guild. A new appointment replaces the old one.
Losing Reputation

#Reputation can fall||-You never spend Reputation, but four things reduce it. Three can cost you a rank and its bonus.||#Upkeep, every turn||-After the opening turns, each guild you have Reputation with takes a little of it back each turn.||-Higher ranks cost more upkeep. Stop earning with a guild and you lose ranks over time.||-The Guilds tab shows upkeep in red beside your Reputation.||#Earning with a rival||-Earning with a guild takes Reputation from its rival, though never a rank you have reached. You cannot court them all at once.||#A demand you let expire||-The Court tab shows the terms and deadline. Ignoring it costs more than the demand asked for.||#A bounty you took and failed||-Handing one back costs your Favour stake.||-Failing one costs the stake and Reputation. Each card shows how much.
Your race

#Services change||-Every ten turns, unless the settings say otherwise, each guild changes its three services. The footer counts down to the next change.||-A service keeps its cooldown while away and shows the time left when it returns.||#Services of your own||-Only your race can buy High King's Decree, Strike Lines from the Book and Call the Reckoning, each marked Dwarf on its card. The Guilds

#Two numbers per guild||-Earn Reputation as you play. You never spend it; it alone sets your rank.||-It falls through rival earnings, a demand you let expire, a bounty you took and failed, and the upkeep each guild charges to keep you on its books.||-You earn Favour alongside Reputation and spend it on services. Spending Favour never lowers your rank.||#The five ranks||-Peasant 0 / Yeoman 100 / Squire 300 / Knight 700 / Paladin 1500||-Each rank grants a bonus for as long as you hold it. The Guilds tab shows your current bonus.||#Services||-Each guild sells three services. Each needs a rank, costs Favour and has a cooldown.||-Prices change with your Reputation: a guild that knows you charges less; one whose rival you court charges more.
Earning

#What each guild pays for||-The Wine Merchants: income each turn||-The Knights Errant: battles won, doubled when outnumbered||-The Grail Damsels: technologies completed||-The Forest Outlaws: successful hero actions||-The Castle-Wrights: settlement growth and buildings no other guild claims||-The Crusaders: sacking settlements; razing pays more||-The Grail Pilgrims: loyal and clean provinces, wins over Chaos and the undead||-Completing a building pays its guild: a forge the Grail Damsels, a dock the Wine Merchants, a barracks the Knights Errant. Higher levels pay more. The building card names its guild.||-Completing any mission raises your Reputation with every guild.||#Rivalry||-Wine Merchants and Forest Outlaws / Knights Errant and Grail Damsels / Castle-Wrights and Crusaders||-Earning with one takes Reputation from its rival once you reach Yeoman there, but never a rank.||#A limit each turn||-Most guilds limit earnings each turn. The Guilds tab shows what each paid.
Bounties

#The board||-Three offers at a time, drawn from all guilds. Accept one to make it a mission.||-Accepting costs a Favour stake with that guild, shown on the offer. Finish the bounty to reclaim it; fail or hand it back and you lose it.||-Finish the bounty for gold and a large Reputation reward from that guild.||#What the guilds ask for||-Targets: land or a lord far from your borders and armies, or one belonging to a faction at peace with you. Taking that one means war, and pays far more.||-Other jobs: hold gold, raise a champion, research, build one of the guild's own buildings, or take captives.||-Or hero work: send your heroes against a named settlement, army or character.||#The price||-Target and distance set the price: Routine, Hard or Grim. An offer changes price until you accept it. Once accepted, it keeps its price.
The Court

#Leading a guild||-The faction with the most Reputation in a guild leads it, whether you or a rival.||-The leader gains an extra bonus. Unless the settings say otherwise, only the leader can buy the guild's finest service.||-It can be taken from you. The Leaderboard tab shows who leads each guild.||#Demands||-From time to time, a guild that knows you makes a demand with a deadline.||-It asks for gold or Favour held with its rival.||-Pay it to gain Reputation. Miss the deadline and your Reputation falls, which can cost you a rank.||#A patron||-Appoint one of your lords to a guild. Select them on the campaign map, then press Appoint.||-Their army gains +10% replenishment and +10% campaign movement.||-You earn 50% more Reputation with that guild, and its services cost up to 10% less.||-One lord, one guild. A new appointment replaces the old one.
Losing Reputation

#Reputation can fall||-You never spend Reputation, but four things reduce it. Three can cost you a rank and its bonus.||#Upkeep, every turn||-After the opening turns, each guild you have Reputation with takes a little of it back each turn.||-Higher ranks cost more upkeep. Stop earning with a guild and you lose ranks over time.||-The Guilds tab shows upkeep in red beside your Reputation.||#Earning with a rival||-Earning with a guild takes Reputation from its rival, though never a rank you have reached. You cannot court them all at once.||#A demand you let expire||-The Court tab shows the terms and deadline. Ignoring it costs more than the demand asked for.||#A bounty you took and failed||-Handing one back costs your Favour stake.||-Failing one costs the stake and Reputation. Each card shows how much.
Your race

#Services change||-Every ten turns, unless the settings say otherwise, each guild changes its three services. The Guilds

#Two numbers per guild||-Earn Reputation as you play. You never spend it; it alone sets your rank.||-It falls through rival earnings, a demand you let expire, a bounty you took and failed, and the upkeep each guild charges to keep you on its books.||-You earn Favour alongside Reputation and spend it on services. Spending Favour never lowers your rank.||#The five ranks||-Commoner 0 / Scholar 100 / Official 300 / Magistrate 700 / Minister 1500||-Each rank grants a bonus for as long as you hold it. The Guilds tab shows your current bonus.||#Services||-Each guild sells three services. Each needs a rank, costs Favour and has a cooldown.||-Prices change with your Reputation: a guild that knows you charges less; one whose rival you court charges more.
Earning

#What each guild pays for||-The Caravan Masters: income each turn||-The Dragon Guard: battles won, doubled when outnumbered||-The Imperial Academy: technologies completed||-The Crow Society: successful hero actions||-The Bastion Builders: settlement growth and buildings no other guild claims||-The Punitive Host: sacking settlements; razing pays more||-The Celestial Temples: loyal and clean provinces||-Completing a building pays its guild: a forge the Imperial Academy, a dock the Caravan Masters, a barracks the Dragon Guard. Higher levels pay more. The building card names its guild.||-Completing any mission raises your Reputation with every guild.||#Rivalry||-Caravan Masters and Crow Society / Dragon Guard and Imperial Academy / Bastion Builders and Punitive Host||-Earning with one takes Reputation from its rival once you reach Scholar there, but never a rank.||#A limit each turn||-Most guilds limit earnings each turn. The Guilds tab shows what each paid.
Bounties

#The board||-Three offers at a time, drawn from all guilds. Accept one to make it a mission.||-Accepting costs a Favour stake with that guild, shown on the offer. Finish the bounty to reclaim it; fail or hand it back and you lose it.||-Finish the bounty for gold and a large Reputation reward from that guild.||#What the guilds ask for||-Targets: land or a lord far from your borders and armies, or one belonging to a faction at peace with you. Taking that one means war, and pays far more.||-Other jobs: hold gold, raise a champion, research, build one of the guild's own buildings, or take captives.||-Or hero work: send your heroes against a named settlement, army or character.||#The price||-Target and distance set the price: Routine, Hard or Grim. An offer changes price until you accept it. Once accepted, it keeps its price.
The Court

#Leading a guild||-The faction with the most Reputation in a guild leads it, whether you or a rival.||-The leader gains an extra bonus. Unless the settings say otherwise, only the leader can buy the guild's finest service.||-It can be taken from you. The Leaderboard tab shows who leads each guild.||#Demands||-From time to time, a guild that knows you makes a demand with a deadline.||-It asks for gold or Favour held with its rival.||-Pay it to gain Reputation. Miss the deadline and your Reputation falls, which can cost you a rank.||#A patron||-Appoint one of your lords to a guild. Select them on the campaign map, then press Appoint.||-Their army gains +10% replenishment and +10% campaign movement.||-You earn 50% more Reputation with that guild, and its services cost up to 10% less.||-One lord, one guild. A new appointment replaces the old one.
Losing Reputation

#Reputation can fall||-You never spend Reputation, but four things reduce it. Three can cost you a rank and its bonus.||#Upkeep, every turn||-After the opening turns, each guild you have Reputation with takes a little of it back each turn.||-Higher ranks cost more upkeep. Stop earning with a guild and you lose ranks over time.||-The Guilds tab shows upkeep in red beside your Reputation.||#Earning with a rival||-Earning with a guild takes Reputation from its rival, though never a rank you have reached. You cannot court them all at once.||#A demand you let expire||-The Court tab shows the terms and deadline. Ignoring it costs more than the demand asked for.||#A bounty you took and failed||-Handing one back costs your Favour stake.||-Failing one costs the stake and Reputation. Each card shows how much.

#Services change||-Every ten turns, unless the settings say otherwise, each guild changes its three services. The Guilds

#Two numbers per guild||-Earn Reputation as you play. You never spend it; it alone sets your rank.||-It falls through rival earnings, a demand you let expire, a bounty you took and failed, and the upkeep each guild charges to keep you on its books.||-You earn Favour alongside Reputation and spend it on services. Spending Favour never lowers your rank.||#The five ranks||-Serf 0 / Kossar 100 / Druzhina 300 / Boyar 700 / Ataman 1500||-Each rank grants a bonus for as long as you hold it. The Guilds tab shows your current bonus.||#Services||-Each guild sells three services. Each needs a rank, costs Favour and has a cooldown.||-Prices change with your Reputation: a guild that knows you charges less; one whose rival you court charges more.
Earning

#What each guild pays for||-The Erengrad Merchants: income each turn||-The Tzar Guard: battles won, doubled when outnumbered||-The Ice Court: technologies completed||-The Oblast Smugglers: successful hero actions||-The Stanitsa Builders: settlement growth and buildings no other guild claims||-The Ungol Raiders: sacking settlements; razing pays more||-The Great Orthodoxy: loyal and clean provinces, wins over Chaos and Norsca||-Completing a building pays its guild: a forge the Ice Court, a dock the Erengrad Merchants, a barracks the Tzar Guard. Higher levels pay more. The building card names its guild.||-Completing any mission raises your Reputation with every guild.||#Rivalry||-Erengrad Merchants and Oblast Smugglers / Tzar Guard and Ice Court / Stanitsa Builders and Ungol Raiders||-Earning with one takes Reputation from its rival once you reach Kossar there, but never a rank.||#A limit each turn||-Most guilds limit earnings each turn. The Guilds tab shows what each paid.
Bounties

#The board||-Three offers at a time, drawn from all guilds. Accept one to make it a mission.||-Accepting costs a Favour stake with that guild, shown on the offer. Finish the bounty to reclaim it; fail or hand it back and you lose it.||-Finish the bounty for gold and a large Reputation reward from that guild.||#What the guilds ask for||-Targets: land or a lord far from your borders and armies, or one belonging to a faction at peace with you. Taking that one means war, and pays far more.||-Other jobs: hold gold, raise a champion, research, build one of the guild's own buildings, or take captives.||-Or hero work: send your heroes against a named settlement, army or character.||#The price||-Target and distance set the price: Routine, Hard or Grim. An offer changes price until you accept it. Once accepted, it keeps its price.
The Court

#Leading a guild||-The faction with the most Reputation in a guild leads it, whether you or a rival.||-The leader gains an extra bonus. Unless the settings say otherwise, only the leader can buy the guild's finest service.||-It can be taken from you. The Leaderboard tab shows who leads each guild.||#Demands||-From time to time, a guild that knows you makes a demand with a deadline.||-It asks for gold or Favour held with its rival.||-Pay it to gain Reputation. Miss the deadline and your Reputation falls, which can cost you a rank.||#A patron||-Appoint one of your lords to a guild. Select them on the campaign map, then press Appoint.||-Their army gains +10% replenishment and +10% campaign movement.||-You earn 50% more Reputation with that guild, and its services cost up to 10% less.||-One lord, one guild. A new appointment replaces the old one.
Losing Reputation

#Reputation can fall||-You never spend Reputation, but four things reduce it. Three can cost you a rank and its bonus.||#Upkeep, every turn||-After the opening turns, each guild you have Reputation with takes a little of it back each turn.||-Higher ranks cost more upkeep. Stop earning with a guild and you lose ranks over time.||-The Guilds tab shows upkeep in red beside your Reputation.||#Earning with a rival||-Earning with a guild takes Reputation from its rival, though never a rank you have reached. #The board||-Three offers at a time, drawn from all guilds. Accept one to make it a mission.||-Accepting costs a Favour stake with that guild, shown on the offer. #Leading a guild||-The faction with the most Reputation in a guild leads it, whether you or a rival.||-The leader gains an extra bonus. The Guilds

#Two numbers per guild||-Earn Reputation as you play. You never spend it; it alone sets your rank.||-It falls through rival earnings, a demand you let expire, a bounty you took and failed, and the upkeep each guild charges to keep you on its books.||-You earn Favour alongside Reputation and spend it on services. Spending Favour never lowers your rank.||#The five ranks||-Citizen 0 / Warden 100 / Noble 300 / Prince 700 / Regent 1500||-Each rank grants a bonus for as long as you hold it. The Guilds tab shows your current bonus.||#Services||-Each guild sells three services. Each needs a rank, costs Favour and has a cooldown.||-Prices change with your Reputation: a guild that knows you charges less; one whose rival you court charges more.
Earning

#What each guild pays for||-The Lothern Merchants: income each turn||-The Swordmasters: battles won, doubled when outnumbered||-The Loremasters: technologies completed||-The Shadow Warriors: successful hero actions||-The Ulthuan Masons: settlement growth and buildings no other guild claims||-The Ellyrian Reavers: sacking settlements; razing pays more||-The Cult of Asuryan: loyal and clean provinces, wins over the druchii||-Completing a building pays its guild: a forge the Loremasters, a dock the Lothern Merchants, a barracks the Swordmasters. Higher levels pay more. The building card names its guild.||-Completing any mission raises your Reputation with every guild.||#Rivalry||-Lothern Merchants and Shadow Warriors / Swordmasters and Loremasters / Ulthuan Masons and Ellyrian Reavers||-Earning with one takes Reputation from its rival once you reach Warden there, but never a rank.||#A limit each turn||-Most guilds limit earnings each turn. The Guilds tab shows what each paid.
Bounties

#The board||-Three offers at a time, drawn from all guilds. Accept one to make it a mission.||-Accepting costs a Favour stake with that guild, shown on the offer. Finish the bounty to reclaim it; fail or hand it back and you lose it.||-Finish the bounty for gold and a large Reputation reward from that guild.||#What the guilds ask for||-Targets: land or a lord far from your borders and armies, or one belonging to a faction at peace with you. Taking that one means war, and pays far more.||-Other jobs: hold gold, raise a champion, research, build one of the guild's own buildings, or take captives.||-Or hero work: send your heroes against a named settlement, army or character.||#The price||-Target and distance set the price: Routine, Hard or Grim. An offer changes price until you accept it. Once accepted, it keeps its price.
The Court

#Leading a guild||-The faction with the most Reputation in a guild leads it, whether you or a rival.||-The leader gains an extra bonus. Unless the settings say otherwise, only the leader can buy the guild's finest service.||-It can be taken from you. The Leaderboard tab shows who leads each guild.||#Demands||-From time to time, a guild that knows you makes a demand with a deadline.||-It asks for gold or Favour held with its rival.||-Pay it to gain Reputation. Miss the deadline and your Reputation falls, which can cost you a rank.||#A patron||-Appoint one of your lords to a guild. Select them on the campaign map, then press Appoint.||-Their army gains +10% replenishment and +10% campaign movement.||-You earn 50% more Reputation with that guild, and its services cost up to 10% less.||-One lord, one guild. A new appointment replaces the old one.
Losing Reputation

#Reputation can fall||-You never spend Reputation, but four things reduce it. Three can cost you a rank and its bonus.||#Upkeep, every turn||-After the opening turns, each guild you have Reputation with takes a little of it back each turn.||-Higher ranks cost more upkeep. Stop earning with a guild and you lose ranks over time.||-The Guilds tab shows upkeep in red beside your Reputation.||#Earning with a rival||-Earning with a guild takes Reputation from its rival, though never a rank you have reached. You cannot court them all at once.||#A demand you let expire||-The Court tab shows the terms and deadline. Ignoring it costs more than the demand asked for.||#A bounty you took and failed||-Handing one back costs your Favour stake.||-Failing one costs the stake and Reputation. Each card shows how much.
Your race

#Services change||-Every ten turns, unless the settings say otherwise, each guild changes its three services. The footer counts down to the next change.||-A service keeps its cooldown while away and shows the time left when it returns.||#Services of your own||-Only your race can buy Friends at Court, The Phoenix King's Regard and Asuryan's Grace, each marked High Elf on its card. At least one is always available.||#What else pays||-A successful court action pays the Shadow Warriors.||#Race rule||-Ancient houses: each guild lets you hold half again as much Favour.||-Turn off Race differences in the settings to remove all this: every race plays alike.
Guild halls

#Guild halls||-Build guild halls in your settlements. The Guilds

#Two numbers per guild||-Earn Reputation as you play. You never spend it; it alone sets your rank.||-It falls through rival earnings, a bounty you took and failed, and the upkeep each guild charges to keep you on its books.||-You earn Favour alongside Reputation and spend it on services. Spending Favour never lowers your rank.||#The five ranks||-Skavenslave 0 / Clanrat 100 / Clawleader 300 / Chieftain 700 / Warlord 1500||-Each rank grants a bonus for as long as you hold it. The Guilds tab shows your current bonus.||#Services||-Each guild sells three services. Each needs a rank, costs Favour and has a cooldown.||-Prices change with your Reputation: a guild that knows you charges less; one whose rival you court charges more.
Earning

#What each guild pays for||-The Warpstone Traders: income each turn||-The Stormvermin: battles won, doubled when outnumbered||-The Skryre Warlocks: technologies completed||-The Eshin Assassins: successful hero actions||-The Moulder Breeders: settlement growth and buildings no other guild claims||-The Slave-Masters: sacking settlements; razing pays more||-The Grey Seers: tainted provinces, wins over Dwarfs and Lizardmen||-Completing a building pays its guild: a forge the Skryre Warlocks, a dock the Warpstone Traders, a barracks the Stormvermin. Higher levels pay more. The building card names its guild.||-Completing any mission raises your Reputation with every guild.||#Rivalry||-Warpstone Traders and Eshin Assassins / Stormvermin and Skryre Warlocks / Moulder Breeders and Slave-Masters||-Earning with one takes Reputation from its rival once you reach Clanrat there, but never a rank.||#A limit each turn||-Most guilds limit earnings each turn. The Guilds tab shows what each paid.
Bounties

#The board||-Three offers at a time, drawn from all guilds. Accept one to make it a mission.||-Accepting costs a Favour stake with that guild, shown on the offer. Finish the bounty to reclaim it; fail or hand it back and you lose it.||-Finish the bounty for gold and a large Reputation reward from that guild.||#What the guilds ask for||-Targets: land or a lord far from your borders and armies, or one belonging to a faction at peace with you. Taking that one means war, and pays far more.||-Other jobs: hold gold, raise a champion, research, build one of the guild's own buildings, or take captives.||-Or hero work: send your heroes against a named settlement, army or character.||#The price||-Target and distance set the price: Routine, Hard or Grim. An offer changes price until you accept it. Once accepted, it keeps its price.
The Court

#Leading a guild||-The faction with the most Reputation in a guild leads it, whether you or a rival.||-The leader gains an extra bonus. Unless the settings say otherwise, only the leader can buy the guild's finest service.||-It can be taken from you. The Leaderboard tab shows who leads each guild.||#Demands||-From time to time, a guild that knows you makes a demand with a deadline.||-It asks for gold or Favour held with its rival.||-Pay it to gain Reputation. Miss the deadline and you lose nothing: no Skaven expected you to keep your promise.||#A patron||-Appoint one of your lords to a guild. Select them on the campaign map, then press Appoint.||-Their army gains +10% replenishment and +10% campaign movement.||-You earn 50% more Reputation with that guild, and its services cost up to 10% less.||-One lord, one guild. A new appointment replaces the old one.
Losing Reputation

#Reputation can fall||-You never spend Reputation, but four things reduce it. Three can cost you a rank and its bonus.||#Upkeep, every turn||-After the opening turns, each guild you have Reputation with takes a little of it back each turn.||-Higher ranks cost more upkeep. Stop earning with a guild and you lose ranks over time.||-The Guilds tab shows upkeep in red beside your Reputation.||#Earning with a rival||-Earning with a guild takes Reputation from its rival, though never a rank you have reached. You cannot court them all at once.||#A bounty you took and failed||-Handing one back costs your Favour stake.||-Failing one costs the stake and Reputation. Each card shows how much.
Your race

#Services change||-Every ten turns, unless the settings say otherwise, each guild changes its three services. The footer counts down to the next change.||-A service keeps its cooldown while away and shows the time left when it returns.||#Services of your own||-Only your race can buy Food Tithe, Shadows of Eshin and Breeding Season, each marked Skaven on its card. The Guilds

#Two numbers per guild||-Earn Reputation as you play. The Guilds tab shows your current bonus.||#Services||-Each guild sells three services. Each needs a rank, costs Favour and has a cooldown.||-Prices change with your Reputation: a guild that knows you charges less; one whose rival you court charges more.
Earning

#What each guild pays for||-The Merchant Houses: income each turn||-The Veterans' Company: battles won, doubled when outnumbered||-The Artisans' Guild: technologies completed||-The Shadow Guild: successful hero actions||-The Builders' Guild: settlement growth and buildings no other guild claims||-The Raiders' Guild: sacking settlements; razing pays more||-The Faith Guild: the faith's causes||-Completing a building pays its guild: a forge the Artisans' Guild, a dock the Merchant Houses, a barracks the Veterans' Company. Higher levels pay more. The building card names its guild.||-Completing any mission raises your Reputation with every guild.||#Rivalry||-Merchant Houses and Shadow Guild / Veterans' Company and Artisans' Guild / Builders' Guild and Raiders' Guild||-Earning with one takes Reputation from its rival once you reach Known there, but never a rank.||#A limit each turn||-Most guilds limit earnings each turn. The Guilds tab shows what each paid.
Bounties

#The board||-Three offers at a time, drawn from all guilds. Accept one to make it a mission.||-Accepting costs a Favour stake with that guild, shown on the offer.
